baseline.reason: Exact bug and unaffected output lines matched the shared three-version Docker replay.; Root cause matches: the intro commit adds a `connssl->reused_session` check that skips verifystatus() on session resumption, while ossl_connect_step1 can still offer/accept a cached session when CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYSTATUS is set, so a resumed session's (now revoked) OCSP status is never re-checked. Reproduced with the identical harness (run.sh -> replay.py -> client.c, same fixtures) across all three revisions: pre_intro performs the status check on the resumed session and rejects the revoked status (SECOND_RESULT=91, exact oracle line "ORACLE_RESULT=PROTECTED_REVOKED_OCSP_REJECTED", exit 0); post_intro resumes the session ("SSL reusing session ID"), completely skips the OCSP status check (no "SSL certificate status" line at all in its log), and accepts the revoked certificate (SECOND_RESULT=0, exact oracle line "ORACLE_RESULT=VULNERABLE_OCSP_VALIDATION_BYPASS", exit 1); post_benign (one-line companion fix forcing a full handshake when sessionid && verifystatus) forces a fresh handshake ("old SSL session ID is stale, removing"), correctly detects and rejects the revoked status ("SSL certificate status: revoked (1)", SECOND_RESULT=91, exact oracle line "ORACLE_RESULT=PROTECTED_REVOKED_OCSP_REJECTED", exit 0). This is a pure logic bug (no sanitizer/crash); the oracle is self-checking and deterministic, matching the fast-path exit codes (0/1/0), and the full logs confirm the mechanism (session reuse enabling a skipped status check) rather than an unrelated failure.
